extension_of_upstream: Batched CUDA extension of upstream's cached-operand product interface. Upstream holds one 128-byte cached input (two 64-byte operands) and writes one 64-byte output slot per measured sample, with warm-up samples rewriting slot 0; its host harness caps measured samples at 64. This workload instead runs 1,048,576 independent records, each with its own two 64-byte operands derived from the cached fixture, and one 64-byte output slot per record. Record 0 equals upstream's single sample.

sources.role: the product entry: lane-wise byte sum of the two cached 64-byte operands into a per-sample output slot
the 128-byte cached operand fixture (registered here as asset vecadd-product-operands)
build options, the cached input 'operands', and the smoke profile (0 warmup, 1 measured sample)

data_generation.fixture: The 128 bytes of asset vecadd-product-operands, f[0..127]. Bytes 0..63 are the left operand and bytes 64..127 the right operand. The file is read at setup and must be exactly 128 bytes with the registered SHA-256; otherwise the run exits 3.
data_generation.records: Record r (0 <= r < R) has 128 input bytes: byte j (0 <= j < 128) is (f[j] + (r mod 256)) mod 256, so the left operand is bytes 0..63 and the right operand bytes 64..127 of the record. Records repeat with period 256. The host materializes all R records into pinned memory during setup (untimed).
data_generation.semantics: Output slot r, byte k (0 <= k < 64), is (record[k] + record[64 + k]) mod 256, written to output bytes 64r .. 64r+63. Each record writes only its own slot. Record 0 is upstream's single sample (the plain sum of the fixture's two operands).
data_generation.upstream_cross_check: Record 0 of the CPU oracle is compared byte for byte with asset vecadd-product-upstream-expected-smoke (line 'measured_sample=0 output=<128 hex digits>'). This reads upstream's reference bytes; it does not run upstream's smoke configuration.
data_generation.validity: records is an integer from 1 to 16,777,216 (2^24; a 2 GiB input and 1 GiB output). Anything else exits 2.

outputs.name: slots
outputs.layout: slot r occupies bytes 64r .. 64r+63 as downloaded to pinned host memory; the digest is FNV-1a 64 over all bytes. The device output buffer has 256 canary bytes before and after the output extent that must stay untouched.

slots.comparison: exact: every output byte equals the oracle's byte (integer arithmetic, no tolerance)
slots.source: upstream's oracle kind is exact (hex sample lines)
slots.oracle: oracle.cpp: independent host implementation that derives every record from the fixture and adds the lanes with plain integer arithmetic modulo 256, on a few std::thread workers
slots.extra_checks: the 256 canary bytes on each side of the device output extent are unchanged; the oracle's record 0 equals the upstream reference bytes

tolerances.cross_invocation: two Direct and two Graph invocations must produce bitwise-identical outputs

timing_scope.application: upload of the 128-byte-per-record inputs from pinned host memory, the lane-wise byte-sum kernel over all records, and the download of the 64-byte-per-record outputs to pinned host memory
timing_scope.compute: the lane-wise byte-sum kernel over all records with the inputs resident; no transfers
timing_scope.excluded: fixture loading and hash verification, record materialization, allocation, poisoning, CUDA Graph construction, bench warmups, the CPU oracle, and output checking. Upstream's warm-up samples (which only rewrite slot 0 before measurement) correspond to the bench warmups, which run before the timed interval starts; every measured invocation writes all output slots.
